title: Strict-transform chart comparison
statement:
Define

$$
\overline\sigma_a\colon
C_a^{\mathrm{st}}(A,B,I)\longrightarrow B[IB/b]
$$

to be the map induced by $\sigma_a$ on the power-torsion quotient.

blueprint_notes.label: status
blueprint_notes.text:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,
and the pullback square
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_strictTransformOpen` — so the
strict-transform chart rings and their cocycle are never assembled by hand.

split_report.summary: Definition split, with no new nodes and unchanged statement. Retained the original map and strict-chart quotient definitions; added the existing theorem that the map is a B-algebra homomorphism and the existing kernel-identification theorem as well-definedness dependencies. On quotient classes set sigma-bar([z])=sigma(z): if z-z-prime belongs to the power-torsion ideal, the kernel theorem gives sigma(z-z-prime)=0, hence independence of representatives; ring operations and B-scalars descend from sigma. The report writes out this elementary construction. All Mathlib searches were run through msearch.py; generic quotient lifts require the supplied vanishing theorem and are not an exact match for this entire chart-specific definition. The requested split is delivered rather than a renewed attachment claim. Repair of the 2026-10-21 return at 8f6cf6cef31: reread all four current cited statements. The revised chart-ring definition specifies alpha as the structural image of a in C and T=Gamma_(alpha)(C) as an ideal; the existing kernel statement identifies exactly this T with ker(sigma). Construct the same quotient map [z] to sigma(z), with no new hypothesis, statement change or node. The report records the current citations and the revalidation.
